# Independent audit: sampled touching majorants and signed logarithmic bound

Source: `candidate 87de5b3c068291f1`.
Full independent read of Sections1–8: **PASS. No correction identified.**
Reran `supporting computation verify_sampled_touching_majorants_defect_transport.py`:
**18,641 exact checks PASS**. I independently derived the main proof before
reading the finished source; the signed-shell normalization agrees.

## 1. Finite slopes and their uniform bound

At an old interior mark, every continuous supergradient is bounded by its
value divided by an interior-ball radius: evaluate its supporting plane at
the opposite radius point and use positivity. Interior convergence controls
all sampled maxima using a fixed inner ball and the opposite-ray concavity
argument. These bounds do not assume convergence of the original parameters
on fiber boundaries or between integer bases.

The actual support supremum phi_z is sampled concave. Choosing each fiber
maximizer and taking an actual anchored convex combination proves the Farkas
inequalities at the source. Thus the finite base-slope LP is feasible even
at a boundary base. This is a sampled majorant, not an ambient supporting
plane for an arbitrary unsampled extension.

For the minimum-norm feasible slope, the projection normal cone puts the
slope in the cone of active inward constraint normals. Conic elimination
reduces to independent active rows, and the printed pseudoinverse formula
therefore bounds it by a fixed matrix constant times the right-hand sides.
No Slater condition is required. Zero normals, lower relative base rank,
redundancy and changing active sets cause no gap.

## 2. Positive finite-plane envelope and its boundary limit

Each plane majorizes every sampled fiber and touches its assigned mark.
Taking their minimum retains equality at ALL old marks, because all the
other planes also majorize the current parameter there. Positivity on the
canonical hull follows from the positivity of EACH affine plane on all
sampled points. Ambient domination of the old parameter is not asserted.

Along every coefficient subsequence, the limiting envelope dominates L on
old fiber interiors and hence on their boundaries by continuity, and touches
the old source values. The old multiplicative certificate gives zero upper
bound for the nonnegative integral of log(V/L), forcing V=L on all sampled
fibers. This is a valid use of the certificate before normalization. Its
positivity hypotheses hold because V>=L>0 on S, and each plane then stays
positive on the convex hull.

Every coefficient subsequence has the same S restriction. Uniformly bounded
plane slopes therefore give uniform envelope convergence on S and on the
moving sampled fibers via closest-point comparison. The same bound gives a
common positive floor on a neighborhood of each old fiber. This justifies
uniform LOG convergence on the entire signed shell. It does not incorrectly
upgrade U_t itself to boundary-uniform convergence.

## 3. Exact finite comparison and signed derivative

Current normalization and V_t>=U_t imply int_(S_t)log V_t>=0. Applying the
OLD certificate to V_t on the old canonical hull gives exactly

    sum sigma_i log[U_t(Y_i)/L_i]
      >=M^(-1) int_S log V_t
      >=M^(-1)[int_S log V_t-int_(S_t)log V_t].

The denominator is the ORIGINAL M. There is no missing M_t factor because
the current unnormalized logarithmic integral of U_t is itself zero.
The comparison is valid for lost AND gained regions, with opposite signs.

The actual signed radial hypotheses imply O(t) symmetric-difference volume
and the fixed-continuous-integrand shell formula. Uniform logarithmic
envelope convergence on the shell changes the signed difference by o(t).
The projection reference is merely a continuous extension of the old
sampled integrand; it does not move fibers or row means. Thus the exact
lower coefficient is M^(-1)sum int_(boundary K_z) v_z log L, with positive
v interpreted as inward motion. The source's translated-interval calibration
confirms this sign and can attain equality with a nonzero coefficient.

## 4. Scope of the scalar-envelope consequence

The old marks remain strictly inside their current own fibers. Proper-gap
strictness, all-direction continuity and a fixed positive scalar interval
give the stated local increasing inverse of actual depth at each OLD mark.
The current global maximum bounds its value there, yielding (18). Its
conditional derivative consequence uses monotonicity and a separately
assumed uniform inverse-response expansion; it does not differentiate an
unknown optimizing parameter or infer a depth derivative from continuity.

All calibrations check, including the sampled-only sqrt(z) example and the
normalized downward boundary layer. The theorem supplies a one-sided
fixed-mark logarithmic comparison. It neither proves a Gamma inequality nor
identifies any separately chosen physical and volume transport duals.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
